title: One-Step Forward Sweep Update
statement: Let $A$ be a type, let $x$ be a finite word over $A$, let $q$ be an optional state and $q'$ a state, and choose an input-head position $p$, an integer frontier $z$, finite left and right stacks $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, an output word $out$, and possibly blank symbols $a,b$. Applying the action that writes $b$ at the scanned work-tape cell, moves the work head right, leaves the input head stationary, emits nothing, and enters $q'$ to the configuration represented by frontier $z$, stacks $l$ and $a::r$, and output $out$ gives exactly the configuration with state $q'$, frontier $z+1$, stacks $b::l$ and $r$, and unchanged input-head position and output.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ and the state type $S$ are types
$q$ is an optional state and $q'$ is a state
$l,r$ are lists of possibly blank symbols
replaced:
Consider the forward-sweep configuration of a one-work-tape machine with
(optional) state $q$, input-head position $p$, frontier $z$, left stack $l$,
right stack $a \mathbin{::} r$, and output word $\mathit{out}$. Applying to it
the local sweep action that writes the possibly-blank symbol $b$, moves the
work head right, and enters state $q'$ produces exactly the forward-sweep
configuration with state $q'$, the same input-head position $p$ and output
$\mathit{out}$, frontier $z + 1$, left stack $b \mathbin{::} l$, and right
stack $r$.
